text:
anya: Quick sync after the offload prototype run. Observed a lot of churn when many small tensors hit the staging pool. I think the admit cache eviction policy needs work (LRU seems to lose temporal locality for tiny allocations).

raj: can you share the hit/miss breakdown? curious if it's cold-start or steady-state.

anya: steady-state. numbers from local load test: admit_cache_size=8k, hits=0.58, median_latency +2.3ms per alloc vs baseline. Misses correlated with request bursts.

pat: 2.3ms sounds bad for small tensors. LRU often ejects very recently used tiny keys because of large-key churn. Maybe we need a tiny-size tier in the cache or size-aware eviction (LRU-K or segmented LRU).

julia: +1 for a tiny-tier. Also consider a probabilistic bloom prefilter that can short-circuit admits for common small shapes (cheap memory, false positives okay).

raj: bloom helps reduce policy-hit overhead but leaks can cause wrong decisions. We should constraint false-positive rate and make bloom per-tenant so noisy tenants don't poison global stats.

anya: proposal: two-level admit cache: 1) hot-small fixed ring (for sizes <= 4KB) with simple direct-mapped slots, 2) general LRU with size-aware eviction for larger entries. Bloom prefilter per worker for fast check before consulting L1/L2.

pat: direct-mapped ring is O(1) and friendly for tiny ops. But need a TTL to avoid staleness when patterns shift. Suggest TTL=10s for ring entries.

anya: agreed. also: add a per-tenant admit-weight so Dedicated tenants get higher ring quota. config knobs: ring_slots_per_tenant, bloom_fp_target=0.01, lru_capacity=16k.

ci-bot: perf/test_offload_admit_cache reported 4 regressions on linux-amd64 in the last run. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/7890

julia: CI link shows spike in frag_penalty when ring overflowed. We should gate the ring to avoid evicting entries that would increase fragmentation (e.g., high-frag_penalty ones).

raj: That means admit decisions must include frag_penalty metadata and be usable by the cache. Cache entries -> {decision, frag_penalty, expiry_ts}. When reusing an entry, if global free fraction < threshold and frag_penalty>X, treat as miss.

pat: sounds reasonable. We'll need telemetry for hit-rate broken down by tenant, size class, and frag_penalty. SRE can set alerts on hit-rate drop or frag_penalty tail.

anya: API impacts: allocator.alloc() still returns opaque Lease. We'll extend admit_cache key to include shape hash + lifetime_hint. No change to on-disk formats.

julia: tests: microbench for very small tensors (1-4KB) with high QPS, and a mixed workload that alternates large pinned tensors to force staging pressure. Also a chaos test that toggles ring size mid-run.

raj: rollout: feature flag admit.two_tier_cache=false by default. Enable on canary Dedicated cluster; after 72h validate hit-rate and frag metrics; then ramp.

pat: I'll prototype the ring+TTL + bloom filter; aim to land an opt-in PR and perf test updates.

anya: thanks. last ask: add an emergency fallback so if admit cache logic causes >5% extra pageouts we immediately disable the ring. CI should simulate that condition.

julia: noted. I'll add the fallback circuit and the perf assertions.

anya: great. ping me when the PR is ready and i'll run the Dedicated canary checklist. :thumbsup:
